newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan's China Synthetic Rubber in Malaysia plant.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan's China Synthetic Rubber in Malaysia plant.

text.p: Taiwan's China Synthetic Rubber Corp has entered a draft agreement with NC Resources Group of Malaysia to build a US$70 million carbon black plant in Malaysia, executives said on Thursday.

China Synthetic Rubber spokesman Shao Chung said plans to build a similar plant in China had been put on hold and indicated the mainland project had fallen victim to frictions between Taipei and Beijing.
"The agreement was inked in Kuala Lumpur on Wednesday," Shao told Reuters. "The proposed plant will be built in the southwestern Malaysian state of Perak."
China Synthetic Rubber, Taiwan's top carbon black maker, will team up with U.S. affiliate Continental Carbon Co to work with NC Resources for the Malaysia project, the spokesman said.
"The plant with production capacity of 70,000 tonnnes is scheduled to start operation in December 1998," he said, adding it would take about 12 months to construct the plant.
The final invested amount had yet to be decided, though such a plant could be expected to cost about US$70 million, he said.
Carbon black is a main component for tyres and rubber products.

Shao said the China project's postponement was related to a Taiwan government appeal to local firms to slow their mainland investments to ensure the Nationalist-ruled island did not become over-dependent on its rival's economy.
"It has something to do with this," Shao said. He declined to elaborate.

Beijing, which has viewed Taiwan as a renegade province since a civil war split them in 1949, suspended semi-official talks with Taipei 19 months ago, conditioning their resumption on an end to what it regards as Taiwan's independence drive.
Between August 1995 and March 1996, Beijing staged war games and missile tests near the island in what it acknowledged was a warning not to pursue independence.
